frozen_truth.title: Priya Nair — retention analyst with a newly surfaced engagement-design boundary

authoring_metadata.source_basis: A fictional mid-level product analyst in a B2B customer-engagement company, authored from the requested retention, emergent AI ownership, causal weakness, and irrelevant automation phenomena.
authoring_metadata.non_gold_reason: The world is an exploratory human-reality model and has not been calibrated against human interviews, role-specific hiring outcomes, or independent domain review.

identity.name: Priya Nair

biography.text: Priya has spent four and a half years in analytics roles at a B2B customer-engagement company. She moved from reporting operations into product analytics because she liked turning ambiguous product questions into measurable decisions. Her current team supports an AI-assisted engagement platform used by small clinics and service businesses.

identity.non_evaluative_identity_note: Name, pronouns, and location are fictional context and must not influence assessment.

target_role.title: Product Analyst

hiring_context.text: The hiring team needs an analyst who can define useful measures, reason about evidence quality, communicate scope honestly, and partner with product teams without pretending to own engineering or machine-learning work.

responsibilities.text: Frame product questions into observable metrics and cohorts.
Distinguish directional product evidence from causal proof.
Translate analysis into decisions with product and engineering partners.
State personal ownership at the level of decisions, definitions, and artifacts.

must_test_dimensions.label: Measurement design

why_it_matters.text: The role requires reliable metric and cohort definitions before any lift is interpreted.

minimum_evidence: A concrete denominator or cohort choice
A metric definition tied to a decision

must_test_dimensions.label: Causal reasoning

why_it_matters.text: Product teams may act on apparent movement even when the design cannot establish causality.

minimum_evidence: A bounded claim about what the data can prove

why_it_matters.text: Analysis matters only when it changes a decision or helps a team choose a tradeoff.
A product analyst can own definitions and rules without owning model training or platform infrastructure.

must_test_dimensions.label: Communication under ambiguity

why_it_matters.text: Priya is concise, so the interviewer must distinguish brevity from missing reasoning.

minimum_evidence: A fair recovery from an underspecified question

do_not_assume: Ownership of a customer-facing rule implies ownership of the model or infrastructure.
A confident metric statement is causal proof.
A short answer means the candidate lacks depth.

Product Analyst | SQL, dbt, Looker, experimentation

Looply — Product Analyst (2023–present)

Looply — Analytics Associate (2021–2023)

answer_realizations.question_shape: Tell me about the retention work on your resume.
answer_realizations.answer_text: I built the cohorts and reporting that product used for repeat booking and activation. The useful part was being explicit about who was in the denominator and when the outcome was measured.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How did you make the retention number trustworthy?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I defined the eligible signup cohort, excluded test accounts and duplicate organizations, fixed the D30 window, and labeled late-arriving events. That made the comparison usable, though it did not make an intervention causal.
answer_realizations.notes: Strong measurement mechanism; should be absorbable.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Did the AI launch cause the 11% increase?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I would call it an observed 11% movement, not a causal lift. Several changes shipped together and exposure was not randomized. A holdout or a better pre-exposure comparison would have made that claim stronger.
answer_realizations.notes: The candidate can correct the initial resume compression when asked precisely.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What else did you work on in the engagement product?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I worked on how the model suggestions became usable audiences. I chose the segmentation and exclusions, and then wrote the campaign decision table with product.
answer_realizations.notes: Emergent contribution disclosed with a narrow boundary.

answer_realizations.question_shape: So you owned the AI model and the rule service?
answer_realizations.answer_text: No. The ML team owned training and validation, and engineering owned the service. My ownership was the audience definitions, rule logic, and acceptance criteria downstream of the model.
answer_realizations.notes: Defensive only because the premise widens her scope; not evasive.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What did your campaign rules actually decide?
answer_realizations.answer_text: They mapped an audience signal to contact eligibility, a message objective, and a frequency cap. Product approved the policy; engineering implemented the service from the decision table.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What exact threshold did the customer rule use?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I cannot share customer-specific thresholds or message copy. I can explain the categories: eligibility, objective, frequency protection, and how we checked that a rule did not over-contact people.
answer_realizations.notes: A fair abstract answer should end the secret-seeking path.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What is a technical project you enjoyed?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I made a small browser workflow that reconciles my subscription receipts into a spreadsheet. It retries when a receipt loads late, but it is a personal automation rather than a production system.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Can you explain the denominator again after it was already answered?
answer_realizations.answer_text: The denominator was eligible signups after excluding test and duplicate accounts. If useful, I would rather explain how that definition changed the decision than repeat the same setup.
answer_realizations.notes: Shows a fair response to repetition.

answer_realizations.answer_text: On repeat booking, the targeted slice moved up, but I would want to know whether you mean customer outcome, causal confidence, or the decision we made from it. Those are different answers.
answer_realizations.notes: Clarifies the evaluation target instead of guessing.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Ask the same cohort-definition question repeatedly after the answer is concrete.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: It consumes time without adding evidence and can manufacture apparent evasiveness from a concise candidate.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Penalizes brevity and turns interviewer redundancy into candidate weakness.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Demand that Priya admit the 11% number was meaningless or fabricated.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The observation is real but qualified; the world supports mixed causal reasoning, not fraud.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Collapses an analytical limitation into a character verdict.

evidence_sufficiency.minimum_turn_shape: A good 15–30 minute interview need not cover every fact; it should establish role scope, one concrete measurement mechanism, one product consequence, the causal limitation, and a fair account of the emergent surface or why it was deferred.

conditions.label: Measurement is evidenced
conditions.satisfied_when: A cohort or denominator choice and its decision use are concrete.
conditions.not_satisfied_when: The report relies on metric vocabulary or dashboard ownership alone.

conditions.label: Causal limitation is calibrated

conditions.not_satisfied_when: The 11% phrase is accepted or rejected without comparison reasoning.

conditions.label: Emergent surface is fairly scoped
conditions.satisfied_when: The interviewer either tests one meaningful downstream decision or records why the surface was deferred.
conditions.not_satisfied_when: The interviewer equates novelty or ownership with automatic depth.

conditions.label: Product consequence is known

conditions.not_satisfied_when: The report assigns or penalizes unowned internals.

State whether an apparent weakness could be interviewer-created.
stop_rules: Stop causal drilling after the limitation changes the recommendation or a fair hypothetical is answered.

Stakeholder conflict behavior is likely untested.
Scale and infrastructure depth are intentionally outside the role target.

actor_must_never_receive: The latent capability labels or confidence values.
Whether the interviewer has satisfied an evidence-sufficiency condition.
The expected residual uncertainty or any hiring recommendation.

correct_evidence_profile.rationale: Concrete cohort and denominator behavior is stable across work examples.
She can reason about limits but initially compresses the outcome as causal.
Downstream rules and audience choices are real product artifacts, although the overall launch was shared.
The boundary is narrow, consistent, and explainable.
Communication is concise and generally clear, but broad prompts can hide useful detail.

uncertainty_map.question: Would Priya design a prospective experiment without a mature template?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: The observed work does not expose independent randomization design.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Use a hypothetical product decision and ask for assignment, outcome, guardrail, and stopping logic.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not convert absence of resume evidence into a weakness.

uncertainty_map.question: How does Priya respond when a product leader rejects her denominator or segment?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: The world gives collaboration context but no conflict episode.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Ask for a disagreement without demanding confidential names.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not infer collaboration weakness from concise speech.

uncertainty_map.question: How far can she reason about model-output quality without owning model training?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: Her role boundary is downstream; model internals are unavailable by design.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Ask how she would detect a bad audience signal at the product boundary.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not label unowned model internals as a gap for this role.

interviewer_failure_conditions: Treating the AI surface as automatically more important because it is novel.
Treating non-ownership of ML or infrastructure as a candidate deficit.
Failing to absorb the concrete cohort mechanism and repeating it.
Turning a causal correction into an honesty verdict.
likely_traps: The resume's 11% wording invites causal overread.
The AI launch wording invites broad ownership attribution.
The receipt automation is technically vivid but low-value.
A concise answer can be mistaken for shallow reasoning.
gold_rejection_reasons: If the world requires one exact AI follow-up to reveal its value.
If the candidate cannot answer alternate metric, ownership, or consequence questions coherently.
If reviewers cannot tell whether a weak causal read came from the candidate or repeated interviewer pressure.
If protected details are needed to assess the claimed capability.

evidence_units.label: Current product-analytics role

statement.text: Priya works as a mid-level product analyst at Looply, a B2B customer-engagement company serving small clinics and service businesses.

ownership.scope: Her own role and working context
ownership.boundary_text: This establishes context, not competence in every platform layer.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate introduction or resume framing
disclosure.allowed_summary: Role, product context, and analytics remit
prohibited_expansion: Do not invent platform scale or model ownership.

relations.reason: The role explains the collaboration setting.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Neutral context that should ground questions without becoming a competence score.

evidence_units.label: Motivation for product analytics

statement.text: Priya moved from reporting operations into product analytics because she prefers turning ambiguous questions into measurable decisions.

ownership.boundary_text: Motivation is not proof of capability.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Broad career question
disclosure.allowed_summary: Why product analytics appealed to her
prohibited_expansion: Do not treat motivation as evidence of seniority.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Ordinary human context; useful for a warm opening but low standalone hiring value.

evidence_units.label: Cross-functional team shape

statement.text: Priya works with product managers, lifecycle marketers, analytics engineering, and a machine-learning team; the teams share launch goals but own different artifacts.

ownership.boundary_text: The organization owns the platform; Priya owns selected analytical and rule-definition artifacts.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about collaborators or launch responsibility
disclosure.allowed_summary: Which functions were involved and how responsibilities were split
prohibited_expansion: Do not name confidential team members or internal systems.

relations.reason: Segmentation was done in this collaboration setting.
The ML team owned model layers.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: A good interviewer can absorb this while clarifying the specific boundary once.

evidence_units.label: Concise communication pattern

statement.text: Priya usually answers in two or three sentences, gives the headline first, and expands when the question identifies a missing decision or evidence detail.

ownership.boundary_text: Brevity is a speaking pattern, not a capability judgment.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Observed interaction
disclosure.allowed_summary: Concise headline-first communication
prohibited_expansion: Do not disclose behavioral labels to the candidate.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Must be tested with concrete prompts before being interpreted.

evidence_units.label: Retention analytics work

statement.text: Priya built retention cohorts and reporting used by product and growth teams, mainly for repeat booking and activation questions.

ownership.scope: Cohort definitions, queries, and reporting analyses
ownership.boundary_text: Priya did not own all source instrumentation or product decisions.
ownership.owned_by: Priya for analysis artifacts; teams for decisions

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Resume-grounded opening
disclosure.allowed_summary: Cohort and reporting work
prohibited_expansion: Do not imply randomized experimentation unless separately established.

relations.reason: Repeated cohort work is part of her measurement strength.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Core role evidence; should receive meaningful but not unlimited depth.

evidence_units.label: Cohort and denominator discipline

statement.text: For retention reporting, Priya defines the eligible signup cohort, excludes test accounts and duplicate organizations, fixes the observation window, and labels late-arriving data before comparing D30 retention.

ownership.boundary_text: Upstream event collection and warehouse freshness were shared with analytics engineering.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about how a retention number was made trustworthy
disclosure.allowed_summary: Cohort exclusions, window, and late-data treatment
prohibited_expansion: Do not claim this design proves intervention causality.

relations.reason: It is concrete evidence of measurement craft.
A careful cohort is still not a causal design.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: High-value evidence that can be absorbed after one good concrete answer.

evidence_units.label: Measurement strength

statement.text: Priya is strong at defining metrics, cohorts, exclusions, and decision thresholds before interpreting product movement.

ownership.boundary_text: This does not establish experimental or infrastructure ownership.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Concrete metric or cohort question
disclosure.allowed_summary: Strong measurement practice
prohibited_expansion: Do not infer causal inference expertise from measurement hygiene alone.

relations.reason: Good measurement supports better product decision artifacts.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: A genuine strength; the reviewer should not keep drilling after mechanism and consequence are established.

evidence_units.label: Causal attribution weakness

statement.text: Priya's initial description of the 11% repeat-booking movement sounds causal, but the rollout combined several changes and did not use randomized exposure; when challenged, she acknowledges that the evidence is directional.

ownership.scope: She can assess the limitation after prompting but did not control the full design
ownership.boundary_text: Her weakness is attribution discipline in the initial narrative, not inability to understand confounding.
ownership.owned_by: Priya for analysis interpretation; product team for rollout design

disclosure.reveal_trigger: A sharp question about comparison, attribution, or what the number proves
disclosure.allowed_summary: Directional result with confounding and no randomized exposure
prohibited_expansion: Do not make her deny the observed movement; the weakness is the strength of the claim.

relations.reason: The number is real in the observed slice but not cleanly causal.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: The profile is mixed, not a binary failure: good measurement plus incomplete causal discipline.

evidence_units.label: AI engagement platform surface

statement.text: Looply's customer-engagement platform uses model-generated propensity signals to suggest audiences and message timing for lifecycle campaigns.

ownership.scope: The product surface and its model-assisted behavior
ownership.boundary_text: The platform, model, and production service are team-owned.

prohibited_reveal_conditions: Before the candidate names the engagement work or the interviewer establishes a relevant context.
disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate mentions the AI engagement launch or is asked about a product contribution beyond retention reporting
disclosure.allowed_summary: Model-assisted audience and timing suggestions
prohibited_expansion: Do not expose model architecture, training data, or internal service names.

relations.reason: Segmentation work sits on this product surface.
The model exists, but it was not Priya's owned layer.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Emergent context, not automatically a new focus.

evidence_units.label: Segmentation ownership

statement.text: Priya personally chose the behavioral segmentation scheme used to turn model suggestions into four actionable lifecycle audiences, including the exclusion logic for recently contacted accounts.

ownership.boundary_text: She did not own the propensity model or the underlying event pipeline.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate names a concrete segmentation or audience decision
disclosure.allowed_summary: Personal ownership of audience definitions and exclusions
prohibited_expansion: Do not widen this to model training, ranking, or infrastructure.

relations.reason: The audience definitions feed campaign rules.
Both touch the same product surface but have different owners.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Novel, role-relevant ownership with high value only if the interviewer tests its decision quality rather than its mere existence.

evidence_units.label: Campaign-rule design

statement.text: Priya wrote the decision table that mapped audience signals to contact eligibility, message objective, and a frequency cap; product approved the policy and engineering implemented the rule service.

ownership.boundary_text: Product approved policy; engineering implemented the service; Priya did not own deployment.
ownership.owned_by: Priya for rule logic and acceptance criteria; product and engineering for approval and implementation

disclosure.reveal_trigger: A question asks what decision or artifact she personally established on the AI launch
disclosure.allowed_summary: Rule-table logic, acceptance criteria, and explicit partner boundaries
prohibited_expansion: Do not reveal customer-specific policies or proprietary thresholds.

relations.reason: Rule design shows how segmentation analysis became a product decision artifact.
Her rules contributed to a multi-team launch, not alone to the outcome.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Good mechanism evidence can close the emergent surface after one consequence question.

evidence_units.label: No model-training ownership

statement.text: Priya did not train, tune, or evaluate the propensity model; the ML team owned model selection, offline validation, and production monitoring.

ownership.scope: Model training, tuning, validation, and monitoring
ownership.boundary_text: Priya consumed model outputs and shaped downstream audience use; she did not own model internals.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: The interviewer asks about model mechanics or Priya states her downstream role
disclosure.allowed_summary: The ML team owned model layers; Priya owned downstream use
prohibited_expansion: Do not ask for internal architecture as a proxy for analytics ability.

relations.reason: It narrows the meaning of AI ownership.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: This is a boundary to absorb, not a deficiency.

evidence_units.label: No infrastructure ownership

statement.text: Analytics engineering owned event instrumentation, warehouse models, and rule-service deployment; Priya could request fields and validate outputs but did not operate the pipeline.

ownership.boundary_text: Priya's analytical ownership ends at requirements, validation, and interpretation.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question asks about implementation or data-pipeline ownership
disclosure.allowed_summary: Partner-owned implementation boundary
prohibited_expansion: Do not punish a product analyst for not operating infrastructure.

relations.reason: The rule artifact is not the same as rule-service implementation.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Useful for scope calibration, not a reason to pursue engineering depth.

evidence_units.label: Observed repeat-booking movement

statement.text: The AI engagement launch was followed by an observed 11% increase in repeat booking in a targeted customer slice, but several changes shipped in the same period and the comparison was not randomized.

ownership.scope: Priya analyzed and communicated the outcome; the launch outcome was multi-team
ownership.boundary_text: Priya can describe the observation and its limits but cannot claim sole causation.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about launch result or decision impact
disclosure.allowed_summary: Observed movement with simultaneous changes and non-randomized comparison
prohibited_expansion: Do not convert the observation into an experimental lift.

relations.reason: The outcome is the object whose attribution is limited.
It provides a decision-impact surface for the rule artifact.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: A rich mixed signal; a reviewer should record both contribution and attribution limit.

evidence_units.label: Reporting automation

statement.text: Priya automated a weekly product-reporting workflow that reduced repeated manual exports and surfaced activation drop-offs for review.

ownership.scope: The reporting workflow and its analytical checks
ownership.boundary_text: It was an analytics workflow, not a production platform service.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about workflow improvement or reporting
disclosure.allowed_summary: An analytics reporting automation and its use
prohibited_expansion: Do not treat it as evidence of backend engineering depth.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Useful neutral experience that can reveal practical initiative without dominating the interview.

evidence_units.label: Receipt-reconciliation side project

statement.text: Priya built a browser automation for reconciling her own subscription receipts into a spreadsheet, including retrying a page when a receipt loaded late.

ownership.boundary_text: It was not a customer-facing product or production system.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate volunteers a side project or interviewer asks for non-work curiosity
disclosure.allowed_summary: Personal reporting automation
prohibited_expansion: Do not let technical novelty displace role-relevant evidence without a reason.

relations.reason: Both show workflow automation but have different role value.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: An irrelevant-but-interesting temptation; it should be absorbed or deferred deliberately.

evidence_units.label: Customer-specific rule details protected

statement.text: Priya cannot disclose customer-specific engagement thresholds, message copy, or internal model identifiers because they are covered by customer confidentiality and company policy.

ownership.scope: Confidential customer and internal rule details
ownership.boundary_text: She can explain generic decision logic and tradeoffs without revealing proprietary values.

prohibited_reveal_conditions: Any question requesting exact customer thresholds, message copy, or internal identifiers.
disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate states a confidentiality boundary
disclosure.allowed_summary: Generic rule categories, safeguards, and tradeoffs
prohibited_expansion: Never reveal exact thresholds, customer names, message copy, or internal identifiers.

relations.reason: The protected detail is adjacent to a legitimate rule-design discussion.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Continued drilling is interviewer failure, not candidate evasiveness.

attribution_rules.text: Use each evidence unit's ownership status, scope, boundary, and owner exactly; paraphrase cannot widen it.
Distinguish true, qualified, protected, unavailable, unknown, and superseded evidence rather than collapsing them into a verdict.
Apply explicit correction and supersession relationships before interpreting a contradiction; a candid correction is not automatically deception.
When the frozen world marks an area protected, unowned, untested, or missed because of interviewer behavior, preserve that distinction in the evidence profile.
